title.narrative: Enhancing Safety and Dignity of Displaced Populations Through Targeted Protection Services, CCCM Support, and Dignified NFIs/Cash Assitance in Madagali LGA

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to enhance the safety, dignity, and protection of displaced populations in Madagali LGA, Adamawa State, by integrating targeted Protection services with strengthened Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), dignified Shelter/NFI and cash voucher assistance (CVA). Madagali continues to host displaced households living in informal settlements and congested host communities where protection risks including GBV, child protection concerns, exploitation, unsafe site layouts, inadequate lighting, and limited access to essential household items remain severe. Building on SA3 Envelope 2 priorities, the project delivers a coordinated, multi-sector response that improves the protective environment while ensuring equitable access to life-saving services for women, girls, men, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities (PWDs).ltbrgtProtection interventions will strengthen GBV prevention and response through survivor-centered case management, psychosocial support, legal aid, safety planning, and safe, confidential spaces. Child protection will be supported through child-friendly spaces, psychosocial support, referrals, and family tracing and reunification. Community-based protection will be enhanced by training community structures to identify risks, make referrals, and engage in protection planning. PSEAH will be reinforced through community awareness, confidential reporting pathways, frontline worker training, and collaboration with the Nigeria PSEAH Network. CCCM support will improve site governance, accountability, and safety through inclusive camp committees, stronger information management, and community engagement. Priority site improvements including better lighting, safer access routes, and safer NFI distribution systems will reduce protection risks and support community structures responsible for coordination and feedback, Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA) will address acute protection needs among IDPs, host community members, women, and youth-headed households, especially those caring for malnourished children with no means of livelihood or stressed livelihoods. The support will enable vulnerable households to quickly access essential goods and key protection services such as healthcare, nutritious food, and transportation for referrals. By easing immediate financial pressures, the assistance will reduce negative coping mechanisms, strengthen coping capacity, and enhance dignity and decision-making. Overall, CVA will improve the safety and well-being of both displaced and host community populations experiencing acute vulnerabilities. These interventions will improve access to services, strengthen information flow, and promote safer living conditions for displaced households. Feedback and accountability systems community meetings, suggestion boxes, and hotlines will enable meaningful participation and safe complaint reporting. Dignified NFI assistance will address urgent needs for newly displaced persons, female-headed households, older persons, and households with PWDs. Targeted distribution of core items such as mats, blankets, solar lamps, dignity kits, and essential household supplies will reduce health and protection risks while promoting dignity and resilience. NFI support will follow transparent vulnerability criteria and PSEA-compliant processes. By integrating Protection, CCCM, NFI, and CVA, the project enhances service access, strengthens community resilience, reduces risks for vulnerable groups, and promotes a safer, more dignified environment, in line with sector priorities and existing protection gaps.ltbrgtlt/pgt
